subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw keep this four-layer multi-agent collaboration stack as core roadmap work, split it into narrow core/API/plugin slices, or route heavy orchestration to ClawHub while keeping only generic seams?
rationale: The request changes agent routing, memory visibility, persistent state, config, spend enforcement, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Split Into Focused Slices
options.body: Keep this RFC canonical but land only separately reviewed core seams, budget admission, meeting lifecycle, and plugin-capability pieces when each boundary is settled.

options.title: Core Full Stack
options.body: Accept the broader collaboration stack as OpenClaw core roadmap work and require a multi-PR architecture plan before implementation.

options.title: Plugin/ClawHub First
options.body: Route orchestration and blackboard experiments to plugins or ClawHub while core exposes only missing generic APIs.

recommendation.title: Split Into Focused Slices
recommendation.body: Keep this RFC canonical but land only separately reviewed core seams, budget admission, meeting lifecycle, and plugin-capability pieces when each boundary is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed connection to product-boundary decisions, VISION guardrails, and recent subagent/session scope work.
